issues.description: New command names break the established singular quickmark-/bookmark- naming convention
issues.detail: Every sibling command uses singular hyphenated form (quickmark-add, bookmark-load). The new commands are quickmarks-reload / bookmarks-reload (plural), breaking the implicit naming contract users and callers rely on. Rename to quickmark-reload / bookmark-reload to match the rest of the namespace.

issues.description: reload() clears marks before parsing, leaving manager half-populated on parse error
issues.detail: reload() mutates self.marks in place — clears first, then re-parses. If _parse_line raises mid-read, the manager is left with a partial/empty dict and changed has already (or will) fire. Build the new marks dict first, then atomically swap and emit, preserving the invariant that marks matches disk or is untouched.

issues.description: New Gherkin scenarios are unnamed, hurting traceability
issues.detail: Both new Scenario: lines have no title, while every other scenario in the file is named. Test names are part of the spec and document the behavior being asserted. Add descriptive names like 'Scenario: Reloading bookmarks from disk'.

issues.description: Tests don't cover removal semantics of reload()
issues.detail: Existing test only verifies replacement of one entry by another. The load-bearing contract — that entries removed from disk disappear from marks after reload — is not asserted. Add a test with multiple entries before and a disjoint set after to pin the clear-then-repopulate behavior.

issues.description: Two near-identical command bodies invite a small shared helper
issues.detail: quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload are six lines each, identical except for the registry key and message string. A tiny helper would make the duplication explicit. Optional, but worth considering alongside the parse-loop extraction so the load sequence lives in one obvious place.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the feature is small, useful, and broadly the right shape — exposing an existing reload capability via a command and routing __init__ through reload() to centralize load logic. Two issues need fixing before merge: the new command names break the singular quickmark-/bookmark- naming convention used by every sibling command, and reload() clears state before parsing so a mid-parse failure leaves the manager half-populated. Test hygiene also needs work — scenarios are unnamed and removal semantics aren't covered. Fix names, parse-then-swap, and tighten tests.
